name: Marxist humanism
summary: Marxist humanism reads Marx through his early writings on alienation, treating socialism as the overcoming of estrangement so that people regain control of their own creative activity. It stresses human agency, ethics and praxis against economic determinism and Soviet dialectical materialism, and rejects Stalinism, vanguard-party rule and state capitalism in favor of workers' self-management and participatory democracy. It remains anti-capitalist, critical of consumerism and of private property as self-estrangement.
scope: The current of Marxist thought that reads Marx through his early writings on alienation and makes human agency, subjectivity and ethics central, as the sources describe it: the humanist reading dated from Fromm's Marx's Concept of Man (1961) and the 1844 Manuscripts; the 1965 Fromm symposium Socialist Humanism and its Western, Eastern-European and Third-World contributors; Raya Dunayevskaya's Marxist-Humanism; the Yugoslav Praxis group (Petrovic, Markovic), and the Czech and Polish dissident humanists such as Kosik. The sources set it against the 'objectivist' orthodox historical materialism of Stalin's Soviet Union and against Althusser's structuralist Marxism. It does not take in Leninist or Althusserian readings, and the sources do not make the whole Frankfurt School or the British New Left part of it: they count only individual contributors (Fromm, Marcuse's symposium essay).

abolish-wage-labour.rationale: Marx, Economic and Philosophic Manuscripts of 1844 (archive.org full text), 'Estranged Labour': "Wages are a direct consequence of estranged labour, and estranged labour is the direct cause of private property. The downfall of the one must therefore involve the downfall of the other," and the emancipation of society from private property is "expressed in the political form of the emancipation of the workers."

alienated-labor.rationale: Marx, Economic and Philosophic Manuscripts of 1844 (archive.org full text), 'Estranged Labour': under private property the worker's own physical and mental energy, "his personal life—for what is life but activity?—[is] an activity which is turned against him, independent of him and not belonging to him. Here we have self-estrangement."

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Dunayevskaya, Philosophy and Revolution (1989, archive.org full text), ch. 8 (pp. 276-278) answers Debray's 'military foco': "Marx's concept of revolution—great masses in motion, in spontaneous, forward movement—is not something that can be 'made' from above," and she lists guerrilla wars that failed.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Marx, Economic and Philosophic Manuscripts of 1844 (archive.org full text), 'Private Property and Communism': private property puts "the sheer estrangement of all these senses, the sense of having" in place of the human senses; '[Human Requirements and Division of Labour Under the Rule of Private Property]': "The less you are, the less you express your own life, the more you have, i.e., the greater is your alienated life." It also describes how "every person speculates on creating a new need in another" to bind him to fresh sacrifice.

property-fundamental.rationale: Marx, Economic and Philosophic Manuscripts of 1844 (archive.org full text), 'Private Property and Communism': communism is "the positive transcendence of private property as human self-estrangement"; 'Estranged Labour': "estranged labour is the direct cause of private property" and "The downfall of the one must therefore involve the downfall of the other." Private property is treated as a product of estrangement to be overcome, not as a right to protect.

vanguard-party.rationale: Dunayevskaya, 'Marx's Humanism Today' (1965): "revolutions do not arise in the fullness of time to establish a party machine, but to reconstruct society on a human foundation"; the party principle rests on "the dogma of 'the backwardness of the masses'" that the masses must be "ordered about, managed, 'led.'" workplace-democracy.rationale: Dunayevskaya, Philosophy and Revolution (1989, archive.org full text), ch. 1 (p. 39) presents "workers' control of production through Workers' Councils" in 1956 as a new decentralized, non-statist form; ch. 5 (pp. 167, 186-187) says the Hungarian councils wanted "themselves to rule over production instead of being subject to the 'norms' set by their rulers" and calls workers' control "the workers' solution."

missingStatements.text: Under capitalism, relations between people take the form of relations between things, so that economic forces seem to rule human beings.

missingStatements.text: A socialist society should be judged by whether it frees people's creative activity, not only by who owns the means of production.
missingStatements.rationale: Fromm argues Marx would reject a state acting as capitalist employer, since his critique targeted the enslavement of people by their own creations.

notes: Strands differ: Johnson-Forest and Praxis writers hold workers' self-management and anti-vanguardism firmly, while Frankfurt-linked and existentialist writers are more ambivalent. Most statements on modern social issues are inferred.
